identity.title: LER 2024-004-01 for South Texas Project, Units 1 and 2, Loss of Offsite Power Resulting in Unit 1 Automatic Reactor Trip and Actuation of Emergency Diesel Generators and Auxiliary Feedwater Pumps

cause.proximate_text: A Transmission Distribution Service Provider (TDSP) had not established and implemented adequate management controls governing design changes to equipment in the Switchyard to ensure that changes were consistent with design requirements and aligned with requirements and recommendations of applicable Industry Standards; and subsequently, STPNOC did not rigorously implement management controls during the review and approval of design changes developed by the TDSP. As a result, in 2014 the Shunt Reactors were relocated, and their associated circuit switchers were replaced with circuit breakers without adequately evaluating the change.
cause.theme: inadequate management controls over switchyard design changes (TDSP and STPNOC review/approval)

chain: inadequate management controls over TDSP switchyard design changes [cause TBD] -> 2014 Shunt Reactor relocation/circuit switcher replacement without adequate evaluation -> Shunt Reactor RT-2 bushing insulation breakdown -> switchyard fire -> smoke plume phase-to-ground faults -> loss of two independent offsite transmission circuits -> LOOP to Unit 1 (reactor trip, SBDG/AFW actuation) and partial LOOP to Unit 2 (SBDG 22/AFW 22 actuation) [backed up by SBDGs, AFW]
notes: Official cause_code is TBD/provisional per FORM-366 fields; category reproduced verbatim as 'provisional'. Block 13 system field is literally 'N/A' in the narrative since the shunt reactor is offsite equipment owned by a transmission utility partnership, not a plant EIIS system - modeled as non_eiis System per rule 2/6 guidance for non-plant equipment. PORV 1C inoperability is a related but secondary failure not on the main LOOP causal chain (not caused by the bushing failure), so it is linked separately rather than merged into the main chain. No BACKED_UP_BY for offsite power itself since it was the failed system, not a backup. Previous Similar Events section explicitly states no similar events found in past 3 years - no stub LER emitted per absence of a referenced prior event.
